newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen moving sideways, tone firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen moving sideways, tone firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to stay rangebound at the opening Monday but keep a firm underlying tone, dealers said.

"The market's in a festive mood, fueled by talk of a long-term debt buyback scheme. But conditions are slightly overbought and players will be more cautious after the long rallies seen both here and on Wall Street," said Gabriel Armando of brokers Galicia Valores.
The blue-chip MerVal index eased 0.3 percent Friday to close at 603.21, halting a four-day advance. It ran up gains of 4.1 percent in the week.

"Friday's correction might continue sporadically, but I don't think it will be very deep," said bolsa secretary and independent broker Luis Corsiglia. "The market shows a definite upward trend and it's underpinned by very good conditions of international liquidity, with bulls raging on Wall Street."
Traders singled out the steel, textile and petrochemical sectors as having upside potential at the start of the week.
"Investors will also keep an eye on Brazil because devaluation rumors affect us," said Armando.
